data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The batch-criticism mechanism suffers a coverage-debt bottleneck that grows at least quadratically in the number of accepted rival positions: each new rival position requires per-target warrants from multiple foreign schools (O(k) criticism tasks where k = number of active schools), and the batch window has fixed throughput per cycle. When rivalry grows from 18 to ~60, the pending-criticism queue grows faster than it drains, so the criticism-weighted attention concentrates on the oldest, most-criticized positions and newer rivals remain effectively uncriticized \u2014 explaining why almost none retire. A sandboxed Python simulation (simulation_mode sandboxed_python_v1) can discriminate between three rival predictions: (A) quadratic debt growth O(n\u00b2) under unbounded per-position warrant requirements, (B) linear debt O(n) if warrants are capped per position, and (C) steady-state debt if throughput scales with rivalry size. Directed research fetches from en.wikipedia.org on ensemble methods (boosting/bagging dynamics for analogy to weighted attention) and Popperian critical rationalism (falsification throughput vs. conjecture generation rate) would ground the theoretical framing.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If criticism throughput T scales dynamically with the number of rival positions (e.g., schools issue parallel warrants), the quadratic bottleneck does not materialize and coverage debt reaches steady state.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the per-target warrant requirement is capped at a constant c regardless of school count, debt grows linearly O(n) not quadratically, and a sufficiently large T could drain it.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If rival positions self-invalidate or are retired by mechanisms other than foreign-school criticism (e.g., internal coherence checks), the queue drains without requiring criticism throughput to match generation.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If criticism-weighted attention uses a recency-weighted or uniform allocation rather than a criticism-count-weighted one, newer positions would receive proportional attention and could retire.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the growth from 18 to 60 is episodic rather than sustained, the batch window could catch up during quiescent periods and the steady-state analysis would not hold.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal loop: (1) Conjecture generation adds rival positions at rate G per cycle. (2) Each new position requires k warrant-tokens (one per foreign school with standing) per the per-target warrant system documented in the formal harness spec. (3) Batch criticism processes at most T warrant-tokens per cycle. (4) When k*G > T, the pending queue grows: coverage debt D(t+1) = D(t) + k*G - T. (5) Criticism-weighted attention allocates diminishing attention to newer positions as the backlog grows, so positions added late in the growth phase receive near-zero criticism probability per cycle. (6) Retirement requires sufficient accumulated criticism to exceed a threshold, but if attention concentrates on the oldest 18 positions (from the initial rivalry set), positions 19\u201360 never accumulate enough criticism to retire. This is analogous to a token-economy budget pressure (SRC_001) where token cost creates selection pressure on candidate artifacts \u2014 here, the criticism-token budget is exhausted by the oldest rivals. The token-budget constraint is structurally identical: fixed supply (T per batch), growing demand (k per new rival), and non-uniform allocation (weighted attention favoring incumbents).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
